NDT training in Beaumont: how it works for Beaumont employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training for Beaumont and Golden Triangle employers and technicians, live online or onsite at your facility, under ASNT Level III oversight. There is no Atlantis classroom in Beaumont. Your employer's written practice governs certification, and a Level III gives the exams. The courses cover UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET for refinery turnarounds, LNG and petrochemical construction, fabrication and marine work along the Sabine-Neches Waterway.

The Golden Triangle (Beaumont, Port Arthur and Orange) is one of the most concentrated refining and export regions in North America. Beaumont's own work is only part of it. Crews here also move between Port Arthur refineries, new petrochemical and LNG construction toward Orange and Sabine Pass, and fabrication and marine yards along the waterway. Technicians who do well in the Golden Triangle can handle both construction-phase weld inspection and in-service integrity inspection, and they keep certification files that pass a contractor audit on short notice.

This section adds depth beyond the summary above. It covers methods matched to Golden Triangle scopes, a step-by-step SNT-TC-1A path, flexible delivery for crews that travel from site to site, the Texas radiography rules, and support for local NDT companies building their programmes. Request a Beaumont training quote whenever you are ready.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Beaumont

All courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Level I covers set-up and examination to written instructions. Level II covers calibration, interpretation, evaluation and reporting. Level III preparation covers the Basic and method exams and the procedure-writing skills needed to run a programme. Recommended hours are in our training-requirements matrix.

Golden Triangle construction projects put steady weight on RT, PAUT and PT, especially on stainless and low-temperature materials. The refineries, meanwhile, need UT thickness, VT and MT every turnaround. Technicians planning a long career in the region usually aim for Level II in both groups. Senior technicians who want to own procedures and certify others can follow ASNT Level III training.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Beaumont, step by step

  1. Written practice. Your employer's SNT-TC-1A written practice sets the requirements for each method and level.
  2. Formal training. Classroom hours, online or onsite. See the requirements matrix.
  3. Experience. Supervised, documented hours on real work. Turnarounds and construction projects both count, as long as the hours are logged against the right method.
  4. General exam. Written principles exam.
  5. Specific exam. Written exam on the employer's procedures and the codes the crew works to, such as ASME Section V, ASME B31.3 piping and API 1104 pipeline welding.
  6. Practical exam. Hands-on examination of real flawed specimens with a Level III observing.
  7. Vision exam. Every year.
  8. Certification. Issued by the employer, and only valid while you work there.
  9. Recertification. At the interval your written practice sets.

Beaumont technicians often work for more than one contractor in a year. Our SNT-TC-1A guide explains how to keep training and experience records that a new employer can accept quickly.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Beaumont crews

  • Live online. Instructor-led theory that technicians can attend from home between rotations or from a site office. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility. An instructor teaches at your Beaumont, Port Arthur, Nederland or Orange facility, using your equipment, reference standards and procedures, and can give practical exams with Level III oversight.
  • Blended. Online theory, then a short onsite practical and exam session.

In the Golden Triangle, turnaround season and construction milestones set the schedule. We plan around both, putting theory in the weeks before a big outage or project phase and timing practical exams so technicians are certified before they mobilise. Ask about onsite training for your Beaumont crew. Cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Beaumont

Refining. ExxonMobil's Beaumont refinery was expanded in 2023 and is now among the largest in the United States. Port Arthur, next door, has the Motiva refinery (the country's largest by capacity) plus TotalEnergies and Valero refineries. Turnaround inspection follows API inspection codes for vessels, piping and tanks, with ASME Section V for NDT technique.

LNG and petrochemical construction. Export LNG terminals and large new chemical projects on the Texas side of Sabine Pass and near Orange have generated years of construction-phase weld inspection. That work includes stainless and nickel-alloy cryogenic piping, thick-wall vessels and very large amounts of piping radiography and PAUT. Construction work is inspected to ASME B31.3 and the project specification, and contractors want technicians who can move straight onto an encoded-UT or digital-RT workflow.

Chemicals and polymers. Chemical and polymer plants around Beaumont and Port Neches add routine mechanical-integrity inspection and their own turnaround cycles.

Port and marine. The Port of Beaumont and the Sabine-Neches Waterway support marine terminals, barge and vessel repair, and structural fabrication. Marine repair work may follow classification-society rules in addition to the employer's NDT programme.

Pipelines and storage. Crude and product pipelines and large tank terminals bring API 1104 weld inspection, tank-floor and shell surveys, and operator-qualification requirements that are separate from NDT certification.

Radiography licensing in Texas. Texas is an NRC Agreement State. The Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS) Radiation Control Program licenses industrial radiography and sets training, examination and certification rules for radiographers and trainees under 25 TAC §289.255. On crowded construction sites, radiography often has to be done at night or inside strict barricades. That is one reason Golden Triangle projects use PAUT where the code and client allow. ASNT RT certification covers technique and interpretation. It doesn't replace the Texas radiographer requirements.

What local employers ask for. Contractors want Level II in at least one volumetric method, surface-method certifications, site safety and TWIC credentials where port access needs them, and complete records. Some roles also ask for API or AWS inspector credentials, which candidates earn separately. Atlantis trains ASNT methods.

Level III services and written practices for Beaumont NDT companies

Growing inspection companies in the Golden Triangle usually hit the same wall. A large client asks for the written practice, Level III credentials and certification records, and the programme hasn't kept up with the company's growth. Atlantis helps with:

  • Written-practice development to SNT-TC-1A, covering the methods you sell.
  • Outside Level III services, including exam administration, review of procedures and technique sheets for the codes you work to, and records audits.
  • Corporate programmes to bring several technicians to Level II before a large project or turnaround.

Book a Level III consultation before your next pre-qualification package goes out.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in five environments, including an oil and gas site, a welding workshop and a storage tank. Technicians can rehearse set-up, scanning and evaluation until the steps are routine. The simulator is only for practice. The practical exam still uses real specimens and real equipment, with a Level III watching.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who writes the course content and provides the Level III oversight for exams.

Construction-phase versus in-service NDT in the Golden Triangle

Beaumont is unusual because two quite different kinds of inspection work go on side by side. One is new construction, the big petrochemical and LNG projects on the Sabine-Neches Waterway. The other is in-service inspection of refineries and chemical plants that have run for decades. Many technicians move between the two over a career. The skills overlap, but they are not the same, and training works better when it reflects the difference.

Construction-phase inspection. On a construction project, NDT confirms that new welds meet the design code and the project specification before the system is pressure-tested and handed over. The volume is high and repetitive: thousands of piping butt welds, many of them stainless or alloy for cryogenic or corrosive service, examined to the percentage and acceptance criteria in ASME B31.3 and the project specification. Radiography has always done much of this work, but PAUT with encoded data is now used widely where the code and client allow, because it avoids long radiation exclusion zones on crowded sites. Construction technicians need speed, consistency, good weld-defect recognition and disciplined reporting that ties every examination to a weld map and traceability records.

In-service inspection. In an operating refinery, NDT is about finding and measuring damage: wall loss, pitting, cracking and corrosion under insulation. Technicians collect the data that API-certified inspectors use to set corrosion rates and inspection intervals. The work is less repetitive and needs more judgement. Examples are choosing thickness grid spacing, recognising when a reading doesn't make sense, and knowing when to call in a more capable method. UT thickness, VT, MT and ET are daily tools, with PAUT and TOFD used for crack detection and sizing.

Training for both. For construction-heavy employers, our onsite programmes focus on weld-defect interpretation in RT and PAUT, the acceptance criteria in the project codes, and PT on stainless. For turnaround and integrity contractors, the focus moves to thickness and corrosion techniques, damage-mechanism awareness and exchanger ET. Technicians who want to work on both sides can do Level II certification in both groups of methods under one written practice.

Moving between them. When a large construction project finishes, many technicians move to turnaround and integrity work, and that is when method gaps show up. Planning that move by adding UT thickness and VT to a construction RT technician, or PAUT to an integrity UT technician, keeps skilled people working in the region. Ask about crossover training for your Beaumont crew.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Beaumont

How do I get NDT certified in Beaumont?

Complete formal training, build documented experience, pass the general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and pass the vision test. Your employer then certifies you under its SNT-TC-1A written practice.

Can I take NDT training online in Texas?

Yes, the theory part. The practical exam has to be done hands-on, and we can arrange it onsite at your employer's facility.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on the classroom hours and experience your written practice requires. SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums are in our requirements matrix. Experience usually sets the timeline.

Do I need a license for radiography in Texas?

Yes. The Texas DSHS Radiation Control Program licenses radiography companies and sets requirements for radiographers and trainees. ASNT RT certification alone doesn't qualify you to handle sources.

What does NDT training cost in Beaumont?

It depends on methods, levels, group size and delivery format. We quote each request, and cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Beaumont employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the usual basis for NDT personnel qualification in Golden Triangle refining, petrochemicals and construction. Client specifications and your employer's written practice set the details.

Is construction or turnaround work better for building experience?

Both count. Construction builds weld-inspection experience in RT, PAUT and PT. Turnarounds build thickness, VT, MT and ET experience. Many technicians do both over a year.

Do I need PT for LNG work?

Often, yes. Stainless and nickel-alloy cryogenic piping calls for PT and volumetric methods, so PT Level II is a useful addition.

Does Atlantis train for API or AWS inspector exams?

No. We offer ASNT SNT-TC-1A method training only. Candidates earn other credentials separately if an employer asks for them.

Can training happen at our Port Arthur or Orange facility?

Yes. Onsite training and exams can be delivered at your facility anywhere in the Golden Triangle.

What do NDT technicians earn around Beaumont?

It depends on level, methods and overtime. See our NDT salary guide for published ranges.

How do I prepare for the UT Level II exam?

Start with our UT Level II practice questions and practise technique in the simulator.

Which codes should a Beaumont construction technician know?

Most process-piping construction in the Golden Triangle is inspected to ASME B31.3 plus the project specification, with ASME Section V governing NDT technique and ASME Section VIII covering new pressure vessels. Pipeline tie-ins and cross-country lines use API 1104. Your employer's specific exam should cover the codes your project actually uses, and a Level III can tailor it to the project documents you work from.

What happens to construction NDT technicians when a Beaumont project finishes?

Many move to refinery turnaround and integrity work. Adding UT thickness, VT and MT certifications before a project winds down makes that move easier.

Is PAUT replacing radiography on Golden Triangle construction sites?

Partly. PAUT is used widely where the code and client specification allow it, because it avoids radiation exclusion zones. Radiography is still common, so many employers want technicians certified in both.
